title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). Over a base S, Grothendieck has two sections σ, ρ of GL(2)_S with σ+ρ = N = diag(0,1). Write Tr σ = w', Tr ρ = w, with w+w' = 1, and det σ = det ρ = v' = −v, where v is a unit. A normal form is σ = [[0,−1],[v',w']] and ρ = [[0,1],[v,w]]. Their images σ̃, ρ̃ in PGL(2) are the PGL(2)-avatars of the generators of the modular group Z/2 * Z/3 used in the study of the 'équation des lacets' (the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations of GT / the Teichmüller tower). ρσ^{-1} = −ε_1 is regular unipotent.

This page (section 2°) characterises when σ̃ is an involution.
(12) The following are equivalent:
- Tr σ = 0, i.e. w' = 0;
- Tr ρ = 1, i.e. w = 1;
- σ̃² = 1 in PGL(2);
- σ² ∈ Γ(G_m), i.e. σ² is a scalar;
- σ² = v·id.
Proof via Cayley–Hamilton: σ² = w'σ − v'. Because σ is everywhere non-scalar (its off-diagonal entry −1 is a unit), σ² is scalar iff w' = 0. In that case σ² = −v' = v.

(13)–(15) A further equivalent condition. Let N'_σ ⊂ GL(2) be the subgroup scheme of τ with τστ^{-1} = εσ for some unit ε. Conjugation preserves the determinant, so ε² det σ = det σ, hence ε ∈ μ_2. The condition is that τ ↦ ε, N'_σ → μ_2, is an (fppf) epimorphism. Its kernel is T_σ = Centr(σ) = (O_S[σ])^×, i.e. the units tσ+u. This gives an exact sequence 1 → T_σ → N'_σ → μ_2 → 1.
Why this is equivalent: trace invariance gives (ε−1)w' = 0. Applied to the universal point of μ_2 (where η = ε−1 is a basis element of O[η]/(η²+2η)), this forces w' = 0. Conversely, if w' = 0 then diag(1,−1) conjugates σ to −σ.

(16)–(18) N'_σ is contained in N_σ = Norm(T_σ). If 2 is a regular section of O_S, every S-section of N_σ lies in N'_σ: an automorphism σ ↦ aσ+b of O[σ] with (aσ+b)² = v forces 2ab = 0, hence b = 0. If all residue characteristics are ≠ 2, then N'_σ = N_σ (the usual torus-normaliser extension by the Weyl group μ_2 ≅ Z/2).

Next page: the condition puts σ, ρ in the form σ = [[0,−1],[v',0]], ρ = [[0,1],[v,1]]. Combined with det = 1 (section 3°) this gives the standard order-4 and order-6 generators of SL_2(Z).

Overall this is a self-described recapitulation of earlier sections IV–V: elementary linear algebra over a base scheme, done carefully in characteristic 2.
errors: No real errors. Two minor points need care. The equivalence 'N'_σ → μ_2 epimorphism ⇔ w' = 0' holds over arbitrary S only if 'epimorphism' is taken in the fppf sense, applied to the universal point of μ_2; Grothendieck does not spell this out. In (17) the claim holds for S-sections only, not as an equality of schemes when 2 is merely regular, which matches his restriction to 'sections sur S'. T_σ is a torus only where the discriminant 4v is invertible, so calling it a torus implicitly requires 2 invertible.

ideas.what: Equivalence of Tr σ = 0, σ̃² = 1 in PGL2, and σ² scalar, for a non-scalar σ over a base scheme
ideas.modern_name: Cayley–Hamilton characterisation of involutions in PGL2

ideas.what: Exact sequence 1 → Centr(σ) → N'_σ → μ_2 → 1, and comparison with the normaliser of the centraliser torus away from characteristic 2
ideas.modern_name: Normaliser of a maximal torus in GL2 / Weyl group extension; non-split tori (O[σ])^×
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (SGA3 for group schemes over a base)
ideas.where_published: general theory in SGA 3 (normalisers of tori, Weyl group schemes); this specific computation unsure

ideas.what: Normal forms of PGL2 lifts of the generators of order 2 and 3 of the modular group, used for the 'équation des lacets'
ideas.modern_name: Representations of PSL2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3 into PGL2 over a base; GT/Teichmüller relations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the loop relations generally; this PGL2 computation is not published

deep.surprise_reason: The author himself calls this a recapitulation of earlier sections. It is careful but standard linear algebra and group-scheme bookkeeping over a base, with attention to characteristic 2. Nothing here is new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'ω'=0', 'ω=1' should read w'=0, w=1 (same variables as on the previous page).
'σ²=ν id.' is most likely 'σ²=v id.' (v as in (4bis)), consistent with Cayley–Hamilton σ² = −det σ = −v' = v.
In (17), 'Où 2 est section régulière' probably reads 'Si 2 est section régulière de O_S, toute section de N_σ sur S est une section de N'_σ'.
In (16) the set is {tσ+u | det ∈ G_m}; the struck 't' is a correction of the coefficient.
'403' at top is Grothendieck's own page number.
